exposure: history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
cohort: The study included 8364 women (age <=65 years) who underwent their first coronary artery stenting between 2006 and 2022, following their first delivery in 1973 or later, using nationwide linked data.
finding: Women with a history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy have an increased risk of a major adverse cardiovascular event following coronary artery stenting compared with other parous women, particularly after 4-8 years of follow-up and primarily driven by women with a history of gestational hypertension.
